Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no external capture.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching a file outside the owned list, changing production code with no tests, fewer than 3 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/video_assembly.py
  tests/test_video_assembly.py
  tests/test_program_audio_clarity.py

THE BUG, measured on real media (same spoken words at three pipeline stages): the speaker's raw stem measures spectral centroid 2200Hz / high-band -27.7dB (crisp, at target). After the program-audio mastering chain the SAME words measure 1098Hz / -48.1dB -- muffled. The dominant cause: process_audio_ffmpeg (server/pipeline/video_assembly.py, the local Auphonic alternative) applies `afftdn=nf=-25` (an FFT denoiser) to the program audio in BOTH its measure and apply passes (lines ~1078 and ~1094). afftdn at that setting smears high-frequency consonant detail. It was added when program audio came from raw noisy mics; the audio now comes from CLEAN grid-aligned stems, so the denoiser is pure timbre damage with no benefit. An independent mastering review had already warned afftdn "can alter timbre"; the owner's requirement is the voice must sound crisp and clear like the outro music.

THE FIX:
1. REMOVE afftdn from the program-audio mastering chain entirely -- from both the measurement pass and the apply pass, so the two passes stay consistent (a two-pass loudnorm must measure the same chain it applies). Keep the two-pass loudness normalization itself (I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11) exactly as is.
2. Preserve the option for genuinely noisy sources: add a keyword argument (e.g. denoise=False, default OFF) that, when explicitly True, re-inserts the afftdn stage in BOTH passes. Default path = no denoise. Document in the docstring WHY the default changed, citing the measured 2200Hz->1098Hz collapse.
3. Do not touch the bumper mastering, the composite chain, or any video handling.

TESTS (tests/test_program_audio_clarity.py, mock subprocess so no real ffmpeg): (1) the default program-audio chain contains NO 'afftdn' in either pass (negative test: assert 'afftdn' not in every built -af argument); (2) with denoise=True, afftdn appears in BOTH passes (consistency); (3) the loudnorm two-pass structure is unchanged (measure pass has print_format=json, apply pass carries measured_I/measured_TP etc. if that is the current structure -- read the function and assert what is actually there). Keep existing tests passing; if an existing test asserts afftdn is present by default, UPDATE it to assert the new default and note why in a comment.
